question: What overhead does the gateway add to 1 KiB buffered and streamed chat with metadata capture, and 64 KiB buffered chat with metadata and with payload capture, at 1 and 64 closed-loop clients, and is its p99 strictly under 0.5 ms at 64 clients at every handoff point with every call answered and captured exactly once?

host.storage: file:// store in a temporary directory on the local filesystem
host.fingerprint: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X 16-Core Processor, 32 CPU / 91 GiB, linux

values.fixture: stub-provider: an instant local upstream answering a 1 KiB buffered completion, a 32-event stream, and a 64 KiB buffered completion

limits.capture: one staged capture per arrival; no drop, loss, or shedding

timing.method: server benchmark histograms: integer nanoseconds from the owning server boundary's std::time::Instant timers, recorded into bounded HDR histograms and read as cumulative snapshots from the loopback metrics listener; each window is the bucket-count difference of two snapshots of one process
timing.precision: 3 significant digits; each percentile is judged on its whole bucket's bounds
timing.percentile: nearest rank ceil(q * N) over the window's distribution
timing.tracing: operator span export stays at its default (disabled); no span is required for timing
timing.assignment: every request carries its closed case and the repetition or admission phase that admitted it, attached when its request span opens; a window takes the observations recorded between its opening snapshot and one taken after its admitted cohort drained, so a late completion stays in its admitted cohort; each cohort's judged-outcome count must equal the completions the driver saw, other outcomes (retried or refused attempts) are counted beside it; a short or extra count, a dropped or out-of-range observation, an unknown label, a missing or negative component, scans that are not the answered cohort's, or a replaced process makes it invalid
timing.measurement: work, wall seconds, and server and driver CPU stop at the admission stop, before the requests then in flight drain; their completions count as late work beside the measured work, and their latency stays in the final cohort
timing.evidence: each window's full opening and drained snapshots are kept under the run's target artifacts as timings/<step>/<phase>.json; the record keeps each cohort's reconciliation and each percentile's rank and bucket bounds

values.workload: one tenant, one wyrd_sk_ key and keep-alive connection per closed-loop client; each client sends its next call when the last is validated; buffered-1kib-capture-metadata: metadata capture, streamed-1kib-capture-metadata: metadata capture, buffered-64kib-capture-metadata: metadata capture, buffered-64kib-capture-payload: request and response payload capture

metrics.boundary: client: calls that ended with a complete validated answer in the window
client: calls sent in the window, whatever their outcome
client: calls refused, timed out, failed, or answered invalidly in the window
server: answer-handoff timings whose outcome is not `succeeded`, counted in their own outcome series and never judged
diagnostic only: client send until a stream's first complete data event; streams only

server: per call, handler entry until the answer handoff (`gateway.buffered`, or a stream's head at `gateway.stream.head`) less the union of that call's own provider waits; nearest-rank bucket bounds of the server's timing histograms
server: the median of the same per-call overhead as `overhead_p99_ms`
server: the median of the same per-stream overhead as `overhead_end_p99_ms`; streams only

server: per stream, handler entry until its final frame handoff (`gateway.stream.end`) less the union of its own provider waits; nearest-rank bucket bounds of the server's timing histograms; streams only
server: the union of a call's own provider waits until the answer handoff; nearest-rank bucket bounds of the server's timing histograms
diagnostic only: client send until the complete validated answer (a stream's EOF), never judged
diagnostic only: client send until the complete validated answer (a stream's EOF), never judged
diagnostic only: client send until the complete validated answer (a stream's EOF), never judged
server: wyrd_gateway_capture_total{outcome=staged}, baseline to post-drain scrape
server: |staged captures − arrivals|, arrivals without exactly one staged capture
server: captures dropped before staging, any reason
server: outbox_events_lost_total for every reason but accounted shedding
server: outbox_events_lost_total{reason=shed}, items shed at an outbox's staging limit, accounted separately from loss
server: accounted bytes the Scribe outbox wrote from the window open to its measured stop, the CPU interval; drained writes are excluded
server: arrivals stopped until no gateway call is active and every outbox is empty
server: active gateway calls plus pending outbox items still present when the drain limit passed
server: handler entry until the answer handoff (`gateway.buffered`, or a stream's head at `gateway.stream.head`), successful calls; nearest-rank bucket bounds of the server's timing histograms
server: handler entry until the answer handoff (`gateway.buffered`, or a stream's head at `gateway.stream.head`), successful calls; nearest-rank bucket bounds of the server's timing histograms
server: handler entry until the answer handoff (`gateway.buffered`, or a stream's head at `gateway.stream.head`), successful calls; nearest-rank bucket bounds of the server's timing histograms

answered requests per measured second
